question.problem:
$$
U=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
question.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of $Σ.$

First, notice that

$$
V=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}^{+}=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{U}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & =V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
